findings.finding:
The static guard over infra/workflows only matches the old `-u user:$…` and `://user:$…@` shapes. It would not catch the most likely regressions of the new design:
- `curl -H "Authorization: Basic $…"` / `--header`
- `git -c http.extraHeader=…`
- `--user=`, unquoted `-u $U:$P`, or `-u` split across a `\` line continuation

The plan also states no self-test showing the guard fires on a known-bad sample.
findings.location: Testing — 'Unit (same file, static guard over the class)'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Widen the static guard to scan `.github/workflows/*.y{a,}ml` and to match a `-u`/`--user "<x>:$…"` argument without requiring `curl` on the same physical line, or join backslash continuations before matching.
evidence: .github/workflows/ contains gerrit-verify.yaml alongside *.yml files
infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh:325 — line begins with `-u "${NEG_USER}:${npw}" "https://${GERRIT_HOST}/a/projects/…`
Plan: 'scan infra/**/*.sh and .github/workflows/*.yml for `curl … -u "<x>:$…"`'
findings.finding: The static guard as specified does not cover the whole class it claims to guard. (a) It globs `.github/workflows/*.yml`, but the repo also has a `.yaml` workflow (gerrit-verify.yaml), so a future `curl -u` there would pass the guard. (b) The pattern `curl … -u "<x>:$…"` reads as a single-line match, but feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh:325 puts `-u "${NEG_USER}:${npw}"` on a continuation line with no `curl` token on it. A line-based guard would not have caught this existing case and will not catch a regression of it.
findings.location: Testing — 'Unit (same file, static guard over the class)'
scenarios: Someone reintroduces `curl -u "$U:$P"` split across a backslash continuation, or adds one in a .yaml workflow, and the guard stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: Scan both `*.yml` and `*.yaml` under .github/workflows. Join lines ending in `\` before matching, or match `(^|\s)(-u|--user)\s+"[^"]*:\$` on its own, and check that scenarios.sh:325 is caught as a fixture.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the static guard to also flag `-c http.*extraheader=…$` and `-H`/`--header "Authorization: …$…"` patterns in infra/**/*.sh and .github/workflows/*.yml
evidence: Plan: 'scan infra/**/*.sh and .github/workflows/*.yml for `curl … -u "<x>:$…"`, `--user "<x>:$…"`, and `://<x>:$…@` URL userinfo'
Approach: 'Fix the class by moving every credential that reaches a git or curl child out of argv'
findings.finding: The planned static guard only matches `curl -u "<x>:$…"`, `--user "<x>:$…"` and `://<x>:$…@` URL userinfo. The fix itself moves auth into an Authorization header, and the most likely regression of that pattern puts the header in argv: `git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic $b64"` or `curl -H "Authorization: …$…"`. The guard would not catch either, so the class could come back undetected in infra scripts and workflows.
findings.location: Testing → 'Unit (same file, static guard over the class)'
scenarios: A later script edit uses `git -c http.extraheader="AUTHORIZATION: basic $(printf … | base64)"` (the common GitHub Actions idiom), which puts the secret back in argv with the guard still passing
findings.suggested_fix: Add case-insensitive patterns `-c\s+["']?http\.[^ ]*extraheader=` and `(-H|--header)\s+["']?Authorization:[^"']*\$` to the guard's pattern list, with one positive and one negative fixture each.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the local and on-box `ps` checks count occurrences of the raw token, its percent-encoded form, and the base64 `user:token` in git child command lines (counts only), instead of just `@rebar.solutions`.
evidence: Plan: "a read-only SSM `ps` sample filtered to counts only (`grep -c '@rebar.solutions'` on the review-bot's git children = 0)"
The new mechanism adds a base64 form of the credential, which the unit test checks for in argv, but the real-host checks do not.
findings.finding: The on-box verification only checks URL format: `grep -c '@rebar.solutions'` on the git children's command lines will be 0 as soon as userinfo is dropped from the URL, whether or not the credential still reaches argv some other way (for example a stray `-c http.extraHeader=…`, or the base64 or percent-encoded token in another argument). So it does not show that the problem, the credential in a process listing, is fixed. The local check counts the credential itself, but the plan does not say it also counts the base64 `user:token` form that the new mechanism introduces.
findings.location: Testing — "On the box after merge + autodeploy … (`grep -c '@rebar.solutions'` on the review-bot's git children = 0)" and the local `ps` sample bullet
scenarios: A regression that passes the header via `git -c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic …` passes the on-box check, yet the base64 credential is visible in `ps`
findings.suggested_fix: On the box, compute the raw, percent-encoded, and base64 forms from the SSM-held token inside the SSM command and run `ps -eo args | grep -cF -e "$raw" -e "$pct" -e "$b64"`, printing only the count (expected 0), with the same three patterns in the local check.

evidence: "sample `ps` and count (`grep -c`) occurrences of the credential, expecting 0, without printing command lines"
Verify-command taxonomy (2) shell-expansion leakage.
findings.finding: The local proof greps the ps output for the credential itself. This puts the secret into grep's own argv (shell expansion before exec), so the check re-creates the leak it measures. It can also match its own grep process and report a false 1.
findings.location: Testing — 'Real path, locally' bullet
scenarios: `ps -eo args | grep -c "$TOKEN"` exposes $TOKEN in grep's argv and matches the grep line itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a small Python snippet that reads the token from stdin, iterates /proc/[0-9]*/cmdline, and prints only the count of processes whose cmdline contains the raw, percent-encoded or base64 form.

findings.finding:
The plan bundles two independently releasable outcomes:
- The urgent prod leak in the review-bot's `clone_change_ref`, whose deploy gates the token rotation.
- A sweep of five operator-run infra scripts plus a GitHub workflow's Jira credential.

The second piece involves a different credential, a different runtime, and different consumers. Each piece is independently testable and valuable. Bundling them makes the prod fix, and therefore the rotation, wait on the operator-script and bash/curl work and its review.

scenarios: A review snag in the bash/curl `-K` changes holds up the merge, and the leaked prod token stays live and unrotated longer.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default for a non-numeric inherited GIT_CONFIG_COUNT (e.g. 'log a warning, treat as 0, write the header at index 0 and set COUNT=1') and assert exactly that in the test.
evidence: "Edge: no inherited `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` (index 0); non-numeric inherited count falls back without crashing."
findings.finding: The edge case 'non-numeric inherited count falls back without crashing' leaves the fallback behavior to the executor. The plan does not say whether to treat the count as 0 (overwriting KEY_0), to skip header injection, or to raise. git itself rejects a bogus GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, so the choice matters.
findings.location: Testing — Unit (new file), edge cases

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the bash scripts strip base64 line wrapping (`| base64 | tr -d '\n'`) when building the Authorization header, and cover a >57-byte credential in the script test.
evidence: "git gets the same `GIT_CONFIG_*` extraHeader environment as the Python fix, with the base64 produced by piping into `base64`"
findings.finding: The bash header recipe 'base64 produced by piping into `base64`' breaks on GNU coreutils, which the Debian/Ubuntu hosts and runners use. GNU base64 wraps output at 76 characters, so any `user:token` longer than 57 bytes yields a newline inside the `Authorization: Basic` value and a malformed header. A bot username plus a ~40-character Gerrit HTTP password easily exceeds that.
findings.location: Approach step 2 — 'with the base64 produced by piping into `base64`'
scenarios: Running smoke-check.sh or feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh on Linux: git sends a header with an embedded newline, and the clone/push fails with 401 or a curl error.
findings.suggested_fix: `hdr="Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s:%s' "$u" "$p" | base64 | tr -d '\n')"` (portable across GNU and BSD, unlike `-w0`).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Run the `git config --get-urlmatch` probe and the real-path `clone_change_ref` fetch inside the built review-bot image (git 2.39) before merge.
evidence: "Verified locally on git 2.56"
"The review-bot image is `python:3.12-slim` (Dockerfile.reviewbot:5, Debian git 2.39), which supports `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` (git >= 2.31)"
findings.finding: The live probe of the extraHeader mechanism ran on local git 2.56, but prod runs Debian git 2.39 in python:3.12-slim. Support for git 2.39 is asserted from the version number rather than exercised: the GIT_CONFIG_* URL-scoped extraHeader and fail-fast behavior are never run in the actual review-bot image before deploy.
findings.location: Approach step 1 — 'Verified locally on git 2.56'; Testing — Real path, locally

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a wrap- and newline-free base64 in the bash scripts (e.g. `printf '%s' "$u:$p" | base64 | tr -d '\n'`) and test with a credential of 58 bytes or more.
evidence: "git gets the same `GIT_CONFIG_*` extraHeader environment as the Python fix, with the base64 produced by piping into `base64`"
GNU coreutils base64 default is `-w 76` (wraps); BSD/macOS base64 does not wrap by default; the Python path uses base64.b64encode, which never wraps.
findings.finding: The bash scripts build the extraHeader by piping into `base64`. GNU coreutils `base64` (Linux) wraps output at 76 columns and always appends a trailing newline. A Gerrit `user:token` of 58 bytes or more encodes to more than 76 characters, so the header value gains an embedded newline. macOS/BSD `base64` does not wrap. The plan assumes uniform `base64` behaviour across operator platforms.
findings.location: Approach step 2 — 'with the base64 produced by piping into `base64`'
scenarios: Linux (prod host or GitHub Actions ubuntu runner): an operator runs smoke-check.sh or feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh. The Authorization header is split across lines, Gerrit returns 401, and with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT unset or 0 the clone or push fails with 'Authentication failed'.
macOS workstation: the same script works, so the author's local check passes while the Linux run fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `printf '%s:%s' "$user" "$token" | base64 | tr -d '\n\r'`. This works on both GNU and BSD, unlike `-w0`, which BSD lacks.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pull the append-after-inherited GIT_CONFIG_* logic out of `_without_implicit_maintenance` (src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:328-344) into one shared helper that both it and `clone_change_ref` call, instead of writing a new appender in gerrit_client.py; state explicitly what happens to the auth header when the inherited count is non-numeric.
evidence: Plan: 'supplied through git's own GIT_CONFIG_COUNT / GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n> / GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n> environment variables, appended AFTER any inherited entries'

src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:328-344 `_without_implicit_maintenance`: reads `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, returns unchanged if not `isdigit()`, writes `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_{base+offset}`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_{base+offset}`, then bumps the count. This is the same algorithm.
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:51-106 `credential_git_env` already parses GIT_CONFIG_* and recognizes `http.` … `.extraheader` as a command-line credential source (line 87).
gerrit_client.py contains no GIT_CONFIG handling today (grep for GIT_CONFIG_COUNT in src hits only gitutil.py).
findings.finding: The plan has the Gerrit fetch child build its own 'append http.<base>/.extraHeader after any inherited GIT_CONFIG_COUNT entries, with a fallback for a non-numeric count' logic. The codebase already has this exact append-after-inherited routine in `_without_implicit_maintenance`, plus a GIT_CONFIG_* parser that already treats `http.*.extraheader` as a credential source (`credential_git_env`). Writing a second hand-rolled appender in gerrit_client.py is NIH, and the two copies' behaviour on a malformed count can drift apart.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (Review-bot fetch) / Testing 'Edge: no inherited GIT_CONFIG_COUNT (index 0); non-numeric inherited count falls back without crashing'
scenarios: Someone later changes how gitutil handles a malformed GIT_CONFIG_COUNT; the review-bot copy keeps the old behaviour, so the env shape seen by git differs between store and review-bot children.

Non-numeric inherited count: the existing helper silently skips the append. Copying that fallback for the auth header means the fetch runs with no credential (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 makes it fail fast), and the plan does not say whether that is the intended 'fallback'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add something like `append_git_config_env(env: Mapping[str, str] | None, pairs: Sequence[tuple[str, str]]) -> dict[str, str]` to rebar/_store/gitutil.py, built from the body of `_without_implicit_maintenance`, and have `_without_implicit_maintenance` call it. In `clone_change_ref`, call it with `[(f"http.{self._base}/.extraHeader", f"Authorization: {self._auth}")]` and set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`. Point the plan's edge-case tests at the shared helper's contract.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the `curl` stub in tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_inventory.py to append its full argv to a calls file, and assert that neither the curl nor the git calls file contains `secret` (the password the git credential stub returns).
evidence: Plan: 'asserts the stub-recorded curl/git argv lines never contain the password the stub credential helper returned'
tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_inventory.py:23-27: only _git_stub appends "$*" to the calls file
tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_inventory.py:67-90: the curl stub sets `url="${@: -1}"` and records no argv
infra/gerrit/feature-branch-inventory.sh:23,94: the password reaches argv only through curl `-u`; git ls-remote at :40 uses `user@` and the credential helper
findings.finding: The plan's script-test step assumes tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_inventory.py has a stub that records curl argv lines. Only the `git` stub records its argv (`printf '%s\n' "$*" >> {calls}`). The `curl` stub just reads the last argument as the URL and records nothing, so the planned check on curl argv has nothing to read and would pass without checking anything. The curl stub has to be extended to record its argv.
findings.location: ## Testing — 'Script test: tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_inventory.py additionally asserts the stub-recorded curl/git argv lines never contain the password'
scenarios: After the fix, the test asserts against the git calls file only. curl `-u user:secret` could stay in feature-branch-inventory.sh and the 'argv never carries the password' check would still pass, because curl argv is never recorded.
findings.suggested_fix: In the curl stub body, add `printf '%s\n' "$*" >> <curl-calls-path>` before the `case`. Then assert `'secret' not in curl_calls.read_text()` and `'secret' not in calls.read_text()`. Keep `url="${@: -1}"` working by placing `-K <(...)` before the URL in the script.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the curl stub in test_feature_branch_inventory.py must be changed to record its argv (and any `-K` config contents) so the no-password assertion actually covers curl.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_inventory.py:27 — only the git stub runs `printf '%s\n' "$*" >> {calls}`
tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_inventory.py:67-72 — the curl stub only does `url="${@: -1}"` and a case on it, with no recording

findings.finding: The plan builds its own append-after-inherited-entries logic for GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n, including an undefined 'non-numeric inherited count falls back' path. It never considers git's built-in `--config-env=<name>=<envvar>` option, which ships in the same git 2.31 release and was designed so a secret config value lives only in the environment.
